name: Online community discovery and reputation index
demand: Hive Index reports 5,857 communities across 36 platforms and 294 topics, with its homepage last updated 2026-10-22; that shows substantial listed supply, not total market demand: https://thehiveindex.com/. Its live traffic report gives monthly topic-page visitor estimates including Entrepreneurship 1,243, Software Development 579, and Artificial Intelligence 455; the report does not specify the measurement month and is publisher-reported, not independently audited: https://thehiveindex.com/partners/traffic/. Circle says millions of members use Discover and thousands search it daily, but those are Circle’s own claims for its ecosystem: https://circle.so/discover. Overall audience size and keyword-search demand for this product are unverified; Google Keyword Planner can estimate location-specific monthly searches, but those estimates have not been run: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7337243?hl=en-EN.
prices: Hive Index currently offers free listings on up to 2 topic pages, Gold at $390/year, and Featured at $99 for a one-time 30-day placement; its FAQ instead describes Featured as $99/month, so that price is inconsistent on the same page: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/. Hive also offers topic-page ads at $50/month; its traffic page advertises a $1 CPC guarantee for month-long promotions: https://thehiveindex.com/partners/paid-ad/ and https://thehiveindex.com/partners/traffic/. These are asking prices and claimed benefits, not proof of sales or advertiser return. Circle Discover listing fees are unverified; its June 2026 listing instructions explain how to submit a Circle community but state no fee: https://help.circle.so/p/basics/circle-discover/create-a-listing-on-discover.

revenue_proof.claim: Historical, founder-reported evidence only: a 2022 interview reported Hive Index at roughly $500 MRR from sponsorships. The same article says subscriptions and referrals had not worked for it. This is not audited, is more than 18 months old, and receives zero weight under the requested rule; current revenue and payment records are unverified.

copy_speed: A direct, narrower competitor is visible in the research window: an AI Tech Communities article dated 2026-09-18 describes a 200-community directory for AI, software, data, no-code, SaaS, startups, and growth, with manually checked listings. The article date is verified; its actual launch date is unverified: https://aitechcommunities.com/how-to-find-online-communities-worth-joining/. I found no verifiable launch date for a new broad cross-platform index since 2026-04-23. Hive Index itself says it has curated communities since 2021 and is actively updated: https://thehiveindex.com/.
platform_risk: High if the dataset depends on scraping or platform APIs. Reddit’s current Data API terms require a separate agreement for commercial uses not expressly permitted, prohibit certain commercial revenue uses without written approval, and allow API access to be changed or revoked: https://redditinc.com/policies/data-api-terms?hslang=en. Discord prohibits mining or scraping its data and commercializing API data: https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy. Circle Discover is a platform-specific substitute: its listing flow requires selecting a Circle community: https://help.circle.so/p/basics/circle-discover/create-a-listing-on-discover. SEO also carries policy risk if agents produce many low-value pages; Google explicitly identifies that as scaled content abuse: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies.
defensible_asset: Potentially meets the required data/network-effect moat if it accumulates a maintained, cross-platform record of verified communities, freshness and activity history, owner claims, and trustworthy reviews; Hive Index already structures listings by platform, size, features, and reviews: https://thehiveindex.com/about/. The moat is weak for a bare directory: public names and member counts are easy to copy, users can leave after finding a community, and the incumbent already reports 5,857 listings: https://thehiveindex.com/. A durable advantage would need original, dated verification and reputation history that improves as owners and members contribute; that advantage does not yet exist for a new entrant.
build_effort: Moderate software build, substantial ongoing data and trust work. Search, filters, structured listings, owner submission and claims, billing, duplicate handling, link checks, review moderation, and freshness workflows are needed; Hive’s current pages show the breadth of fields and topic structure an incumbent already maintains: https://thehiveindex.com/about/ and https://thehiveindex.com/submit/. Agents could handle submission classification, deduplication, permitted link checks, page drafts, billing FAQs, and report triage. Human review would still be needed for disputed listings, reviews, and platform/data-rights exceptions. A niche-first directory is materially more manageable than matching the incumbent’s breadth.
channel: Use inbound channels: original, useful SEO pages; self-service owner-submitted listings; app/product marketplace submissions; and opt-in integrations or partner placements. Do not cold email, SMS, DM, or call. Avoid mass-generated pages without unique value, which Google identifies as scaled content abuse: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies. Build ingestion around owner submissions and permitted sources rather than scraping Discord or Reddit: https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy and https://redditinc.com/policies/data-api-terms?hslang=en.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. The Hive Index about page describes a dedicated team and an independent founder but gives no measured operating hours; it cannot establish that this model stays within Ricardo’s <=5 hours/week: https://thehiveindex.com/about/. That target is plausible only with narrow scope, self-service submissions, automated routine checks, and human escalation for exceptions; this is an inference, not verified operating evidence.
automation_reason: Estimated 65% in a mature, narrowly scoped operation: agents can process structured submissions, categorize and deduplicate listings, check links where permitted, draft useful listing pages, reconcile routine billing questions, and triage reports. Human judgment remains important for disputed claims, reputation reviews, platform permissions, and quality control. This is a design estimate, not measured evidence; platform rules constrain automated data collection: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/, https://support-dev.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/8563934450327-Discord-Developer-Policy, and https://redditinc.com/policies/data-api-terms?hslang=en.
moat_assessment: Conditional pass. A maintained cross-platform dataset and reputation history could qualify as a compiled-data moat and create a modest network effect, but the bare concept is not defensible against an incumbent with thousands of listings. The new product needs a focused niche and unique, regularly verified data to earn an advantage; otherwise it is a copyable directory. Evidence for incumbent scale and structured records: https://thehiveindex.com/ and https://thehiveindex.com/about/.
desk_test: In one desk-work day, choose one niche and use Google Keyword Planner to check location-specific monthly search estimates and bid estimates for high-intent queries about finding its communities; inspect the current search results and Hive topic pages to see whether accurate, fresh listings solve a visible gap. Keyword Planner supports monthly-search estimates and geographic targeting, but requires billing information to access basic features; no estimates have been run: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7337243?hl=en-EN and https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6325025?hl=en-en. Compare the niche against Hive’s own topic traffic and active-promotion figures: https://thehiveindex.com/partners/traffic/. This tests search opportunity cheaply without contacting anyone; it does not prove willingness to pay.
red_flags: No verified current revenue, churn, paid-customer count, or operator-hours evidence. The only product-specific revenue claim found is a founder-reported ~$500 MRR from 2022, which is over 18 months old and zero weight; the same article reports failed subscription/referral attempts, also zero weight under the requested rule: https://bootstrappers.com/how-do-you-monetize-community-this-founder-struck-gold-with-lifetime-subscriptions-and-sponsorships/. Hive’s live traffic report shows most listed topic pages with 0/4 active promotions, while a few have one or two; its ad demand appears concentrated and the figures are self-reported: https://thehiveindex.com/partners/traffic/. Featured pricing conflicts between the page’s one-time offer and FAQ: https://thehiveindex.com/submit/. A broad cross-platform directory risks stale listings, review abuse, platform terms changes, and search dependence; Circle Discover and Hive Index already provide meaningful substitutes: https://discover.circle.so/ and https://thehiveindex.com/.
